items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: I guess it’s the Uncle Tom thing. A lot of them just associate that music with the old days when Teddy Wilson couldn’t find a hotel because he was black or something like that.

ctx.x: Why is it that there seems to be very few African American people in the audience, and sometimes on the bandstand, depending on the style of music.

Yeah. And there are a few. I guess it’s the Uncle Tom thing. A lot of them just associate that music with the old days when Teddy Wilson couldn’t find a hotel because he was black or something like that. And I don’t know who’s — I guess family-wise and friend- wise they’re cultivating that. They’re keeping that going faster than we’re getting them to play in parties and groups you know. I had a call — in my career in Orlando, which is kind of waning, I mean there’s not much going on, you know I used to book some…
